📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific challenges, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest revision, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for revision 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an glitch that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

It has been revealed that this is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an concern that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Industry observers note that team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s enhancement takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an concern that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Sources indicate that finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

Latest Update: Judge denies motion to dismiss lawsuit accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of worsening RAM crisis by fixing memory prices and supply

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
  • The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year.
  • In a recent development, the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

In a recent development, the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

Sources indicate that "But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

Recent findings suggest that you know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which right now looks likely to last until at least 2028.

According to recent reports, first declared over a year ago, Digimon Alysion has finally arrived to offer a virtual companion to the Digimon Trading Card Game, allowing you to collect cards, build your own decks, and follow a upcoming story set in a new virtual world. Having just released in over 183 countries worldwide, the game is now available on both Google Play and the App Store for players to download and try it out for themselves.

While some players won't have access to the game due to conflicts with regions like South America and its gacha game ban, the response to Digimon's TCG release has already been receiving a strong start on mobile storefronts.

Following the release of Digimon's triple-A Story: Time Stranger, Digimon's next entry into a fresh gaming market with Digimon Alysion already had plenty of hype from fans leading up to the release, which has caused the game to already top the charts as the number one most downloaded game in the Card section of the iOS App Store.

Boasting several of the features players were hoping for in the full release, Digimon Alysion offers a collectible digi-dex catalog, PvP battles, booster pulling mechanics, a visual novel-style story, and even a ranked mode to compete against other players for higher ranks and greater rewards as a result.

Recent findings suggest that to reward fans who supported the game before its release, Digimon Alysion is also offering players some free goodies to celebrate receiving over 450,000 pre-registered accounts. All you have to do to claim the rewards yourself is download the game and claim tickets that can be used in exchange for exclusive cards, packs, and other digital currencies.

While there are plenty of competitors in the mobile TCG market already, there seems to be plenty of incentives to give Digimon Alysion a go if you're remotely a fan of the series, even if it's just to collect cards and check out its story rather than go head-to-head with other players.

  • Recent findings suggest that the significant latest arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the latest major content patch has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

Recent findings suggest that this one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

Recent findings suggest that the significant latest arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

In a recent development, varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

Industry observers note that the more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Industry observers note that varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

In a recent development, the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the significant event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Catch up on the latest set of Genshin Impact codes before you play, and check out why we think Genshin Impact is one of the best mobile games you can play today.

Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

In a recent development, this upcoming mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an matter for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming patch, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new set of Nintendo patents has been discovered that have paved the way for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to return on Switch 2, so long as the player doesn’t mind shelling out for extra hardware.
  • It has been revealed that the Nintendo DS was a massively popular system, selling 154 million units worldwide.
  • In a recent development, one possible solution to Nintendo’s second screen matter may have been revealed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new set of Nintendo patents has been discovered that have paved the way for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to return on Switch 2, so long as the player doesn’t mind shelling out for extra hardware.

It has been revealed that the Nintendo DS was a massively popular system, selling 154 million units worldwide. However, the system’s dual-screen design has made it hard for its titles to be rereleased on modern systems. Konami managed it with the Castlevania series, but few other companies seem interested in reviving their DS games on the Switch or Switch 2.

In a recent development, one possible solution to Nintendo’s second screen matter may have been revealed. According to RetroDodo, two patents have been discovered that will allow the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 to play games from the previous console generations.

The first patent allows a game to be instantly transferred between two systems, while the second allows a different console to be used alongside one running a title, with the ability to use touchscreen controls. Taken together, these patents could emulate the Nintendo DS, 3DS, and Wii U GamePad.

In a recent development, the caveat is that it would require someone to own two Nintendo Switch 2 units, or one of each Switch console, to run old games. This would be fine in a household that owns both systems, but for those who don’t, it’s an expensive proposition just to be able to run DS, 3DS, and Wii U titles.

This isn’t the first time Nintendo has brought dual-screen games to consoles; DS games were available on the Wii U, with the GamePad used as the bottom screen. This isn’t the most elegant of solutions, especially as it forces the player to keep switching perspective between screens, but it gets the job done.

The caveat to these patents is that it would require someone owning two Nintendo Switch 2 units, or one of each Switch console, to run old games.

In a recent development, there’s also the question of what games fans would even want to play on such a setup. The obvious answer is the Pokémon games, as fans would crawl through broken glass for modern ports of Pokémon HeartGold & SoulSilver that don’t cost hundreds of dollars on eBay. However, considering Game Freak seems averse to making money, there are still easier-to-port Pokémon games that aren’t on the Switch 2, and the DS games would take a ton of work to revision.

The Wii U also doesn’t have much, since pretty much all its best games are already on the Switch, and they received updated ports over the console’s lifespan. Sure, it’d be cool for Nintendo Land to return, but no one’s lining up for Star Fox Zero. The Wii U was such a bomb that Nintendo is unlikely to bring up its ghost, even through a costly hardware expansion.

In a recent development, the Nintendo 3DS had a stacked library of amazing games, but some of them would lose the system's major selling point: 3D visuals. Super Mario 3D Land was a tremendous game, but it requires playing in 3D to get the full effect, especially for its stage secrets. The lack of Streepass and Spotpass would also take away a lot of the extra functions present in Nintendo 3DS games.

Recent findings suggest that it’s entirely possible that these Nintendo Switch 2 patents won’t come to anything. After all, companies patent ideas all the time that never get made. The ability to play DS, 3DS, and Wii U games on the Switch 2 would be incredible, but the price of entry might be a bit too high for most fans, even if the titles are released for free on Nintendo Switch Online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige has all but confirmed the setting for Avengers: Secret Wars and its "imagination gone wild" premise.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly, Feige described Secret Wars – arriving one year after Avengers: Doomsday as a "launching pad for our films in 2028" as they begin "a very new era at that point.".

2028 will see Marvel release X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3, but in the here-and-now, Feige (usually a brick wall when it comes to spoilers) is happy to reveal that Secret Wars will be set on Battleworld.

In a recent development, not familiar with the location? Taking its name from the 1984 and 2015 comics of the same name, Battleworld was first depicted as a planet overseen by the Beyonder for his goal of making several heroes and villains fight.

It has been revealed that the 2015 iteration is closer to what we'll likely see in the MCU – a jumbled patchwork planet brought together by Doctor Doom after the collapse of the multiverse. Fragments of different times, realities and locations are all able to co-exist in one space, and is ruled by Doom.

"Secret Wars is different than any other movie we’ve ever made," Feige teased. "Look at the comics. The characters and the settings and the worlds within this singular planet where our movie Secret Wars takes place is the imagination gone wild, which is what’s exciting about it.".

It has been revealed that "It’s such a major storyline, it needed two movies to tell that story," co-director Joe Russo added. "Doom as a character needs a lot of space, especially when Robert Downey is playing him. So the scale of the story, the emotional scale of the story is so large that it really needed to be a two-parter.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Feige even went one further, saying the comics Secret Wars is based on (the two Secret Wars events and Jonathan Hickman's 'Time Runs Out') could be used to work out spoilers for the next two MCU crossovers.

According to recent reports, "If you wanted spoilers for The Odyssey, you could go read the book. If you want spoilers for Doomsday and Secret Wars, you can go look at the comics. It is very much the same thing that we’re doing, which is the fun of what happens in the culmination of an incursion, multiversal-collapse event, and what Doctor Doom does next," Feige remarked. "And that very much is what Secret Wars is.".

Prior to Secret Wars stepping into Battleworld, Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US cinemas on December 18.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found unique ways to get around the game’s six-star wanted level, proving it’s not entirely inescapable.

Sources indicate that one of the most interesting things about GTA 6 is how it makes some pretty major changes to the core foundation of the whole series. Cars are harder to steal and drive around the tight roads of Leonida, gunfights have more to them than just endless headshots, and the whole world has far more immersive sim elements than previous games.

I’d argue that the biggest thing that’s been reworked, though, is crime and its many ripple effects. Not only are police more aware of every action you take, but you can also take things so far as to reach a somewhat divisive six-star wanted level and incite a manhunt that only ends when Jason and Lucia are dead. At least, that’s how it’s supposed to work….

Recent findings suggest that the first and most involved way that a GTA 6 player has escaped the six-star wanted level comes from Japanese VTuber Haigure Tamao. As reported by Dexerto, Tamao amassed a six-star wanted level by causing pure carnage before activating the recently discovered easter egg that takes you back in time to classic Vice City.

It has been revealed that upon returning to the present, Tamao discovered that their six-star wanted level had been completely removed. The easter egg itself is very time-consuming and can only be done once, so it’s not exactly a clean way to get rid of six stars, but it clearly does work and means the manhunt can actually come to an end.

I guess it makes sense since Jason or Lucia literally travelled in time. I don’t think the police are quite advanced enough to keep track of Terminator shenanigans.

It has been revealed that the more confusing but attainable method comes from Twitter user Fearcbpr, who shared a video of them escaping the six-star wanted level. In their case, they used the IAA Black Site bunker located in North Mariana County, which somehow caused the six-star wanted level to slowly disappear after some time.

It’s not clear why exactly that method works considering it’s not a reload like the time travel easter egg, but the video shows that it’s a working method. I imagine that’s going to be patched out in the future, but at least we have proof that six stars isn’t quite the death sentence that it’s made out to be.

Latest Update: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • It has been revealed that from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

It has been revealed that from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

It makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

It has been revealed that thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

In a recent development, it's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

Industry observers note that in terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock fresh rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

It has been revealed that between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make new, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that original Story: If there's anything we could add to GTA 6 as things stand, it'd be an official 60FPS mode. That's obviously not possible right now due to how demanding the game is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S hardware, even in the case of the PS5 Pro.

Interestingly though, over the weekend, players have discovered the ability to activate what some are calling a "60FPS Glitch" or "60FPS Bug" on Xbox consoles, forcing the game to unlock its FPS and run at a higher frame rate than it's actually supposed to.

Someone called Meowwie64 on Reddit appears to have found this, and here's what they did to activate it:.

Now, as mentioned, there are multiple drawbacks here. The first one is that the glitch speeds up most aspects of the game, making it run faster than intended (and look like it's in fast-forward mode!). This is obviously not an ideal way to enjoy GTA 6, and serves as an immediate deal-breaker in my view.

According to recent reports, another one is that reaching 60FPS is pretty much impossible under normal gameplay circumstances. If you're driving down a highway, for example, you're likely only going to get around 35-40FPS at max, with 60FPS and above being saved for situations that require no graphical intensity whatsoever.

Sources indicate that and finally, it should be noted that GTA 6 was never intended to be run this way on Xbox Series X|S, and therefore you could run into all sorts of problems - crashes, bugs, maybe even your console overheating. That last one is unlikely, but the game has been specifically built to run at 30FPS on these machines, so it's not worth pushing it in our view.

Tech Report: The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an enhancement on what to expect in 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of newly introduced content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.
  • The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of newly introduced content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s newly introduced blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of problems should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

It has been revealed that the first stage of the upcoming roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Industry observers note that another vital area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more challenges join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

It has been revealed that the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported challenges.

Industry observers note that until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

Super Boss Monster review

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I was a fan of the original Boss Monster, so I enjoyed Super Boss Monster as well.
  • Newly introduced town board ensures players will always have options every round.
  • According to recent reports, why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I was a fan of the original Boss Monster, so I enjoyed Super Boss Monster as well. It’s a superior version of a fun, relatively quick game. There’s enough strategy to keep advanced board game fans interested, but simple enough for newcomers and younger fans to enjoy as well.

Fixes many of its predecessors' shortcomings.

Compatible with Boss Monster and expansions.

Newly introduced town board ensures players will always have options every round.

Can feel slightly limited on its own.

Players tend to gang up on whoever's winning.

According to recent reports, why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

In a recent development, boss Monster, first released in 2013, is a quick-paced card game that puts players on the monster’s side of a dungeon crawl. As the name would suggest, it involves luring heroes into a dungeon and then killing them before they can reach the Boss Monster. Developer Brotherwise Games turned this into a steady franchise, releasing numerous expansions that added newly introduced spells and rooms to the equation.

It has been revealed that however, now that's all been shaken up with the latest instalment – upgrading both the 8-bit pixel look to Super Nintendo-inspired 16-bit graphics as well as its gameplay. Super Boss Monster smooths over some of the rough edges of Boss Monster while remaining fully compatible with the previous version of the game. The result is a quick-paced experience that feels a bit more even than before but maintains most of its predecessor’s tenets. Is it one of the best card games, though?

Super Boss Monster features three separate decks of cards and a town board where heroes go shortly before adventuring to their doom. The first of these decks consists of Room cards, which players use to build their dungeon. Rooms are divided between trap rooms and monster rooms, along with their advanced counterparts. Each room has a damage figure and treasure on the bottom of the card. The damage determines how much damage a room deals to heroes, while the treasure helps to determine which heroes (if any) enter a player’s dungeon.

The second deck of cards is the spell deck, which comprise of instant use spells that are generally disruptive to the game. Most of these spells are cast during the adventure phase of the game and typically impose a negative effect, either by buffing a hero or by somehow negating effects in a player’s dungeon. Many spells are cast on other players, although there are some spells that have beneficial effects as well.

Players: 1-4Ages: 13+Game type: Drafting/hand-managementComplexity: LowLasts: 30minsDesigner: Hayden Dillard & Johnny O'NealPublisher: Brotherwise GamesPlay if you enjoy: Boss Monster, old-school video games.

It has been revealed that the final deck of cards is the hero deck, which comprises two tiers of heroes. Early on in the game, players will face standard heroes that have low health and limited abilities. As the game enters its final stage, players have to contend with epic heroes, which have even more health and can negate entire rooms in a dungeon. While epic heroes are harder to vanquish, they score more points than their standard counterparts.

All three decks were featured in the original Boss Monster, but the one new addition to Super Boss Monster is the town board. Heroes now populate on the town board, destined to either travel to a dungeon or linger in one of several special buildings. Each of these buildings also have minion slots, granting players a one-off action during the town phase. Drafting also takes place on the town board, with leftover cards remaining on the board until the next phase.

Super Boss Monster plays out over numerous rounds, with an unrelenting stream of heroes entering each player’s dungeon periodically. Each player starts with a hand of cards and a small one-room dungeon. Over the course of the game, players build out that dungeon to a total of five rooms and buff it either temporarily or permanently with various effects. Once a dungeon hits its allotted five rooms, a player’s Boss Monster levels up, granting them newly introduced abilities.

Boss Monster plays very similarly to Super Boss Monster, save for the opening Town Phase round. During this initial round, Heroes enter town and the Market is restocked with new rooms and spells. Starting with the first player (a signifier that rotates each round), players then place their Minion on either a town slot (or occasionally on a slot within their own dungeon) and drafts a new card from the market. One confusing part of the game is that the Minion effects don’t resolve immediately – players have to wait until a separate phase to gain their benefit.

After the town phase comes the Build phase, where players add to their dungeon. Builds happen simultaneously and are technically secret, as the results often determine which heroes enter which dungeon. Players choose a card from their hand and play it face down onto their dungeon. Once all players have chosen their rooms, they simultaneously reveal them.

Recent findings suggest that one thing I like about Super Boss Monster is that players don’t have to spend resources to add a room to their dungeon. Basic Trap and Monster Rooms can be played during any round. Stronger Advanced rooms can only be played on top of existing rooms that share a treasure icon with the existing room. Advanced rooms often have more treasure than basic rooms, along with more powerful abilities. However, placing an Advanced room essentially resets that room, removing any buffs from that space.

Recent findings suggest that if strategic card games are your thing, it's worth checking out Wingspan Pocket. It has all the brilliance of the original, but with far fewer barriers to entry. As for a more fantastical strategy game, it's worth checking out Gwent: The Legendary Card Game.

After the Build phase comes the Minion phase, when players gain their benefit of whatever space they placed their minion. Minion effects range from gaining a temporary piece of treasure to the dungeon (which can break ties and entice heroes to a certain dungeon) to drawing extra cards. One of my favorite minion effects is the +2 effect. When a hero moves to a specialty landmark, players can buff a hero with two additional health and send them to any dungeon. Although players can send a buffed hero to an opponent’s dungeon to hurt them, it’s also a way for players to gain extra points, especially when a glut of heroes show up that don’t want to enter your dungeon. This is one of the substantial improvements from Boss Monster, as there are now ways to get a steady stream of heroes into the dungeon even when the treasure doesn’t fall their way.

Once the Minion phase is complete, the heroes finally enter the dungeon. Players determine which heroes enter which dungeon by determining which dungeon has the most of a hero’s preferred treasure type. Players can pursue one of two strategies to attract heroes; they can either dominate one or two treasure types or go for a more balanced approach that relies on careful deployment of minion powers. Both strategies come with their own advantages, although it may be easier to dominate one type of treasure in higher player count games.

Sources indicate that once heroes deploy to the dungeon, players take turns seeing whether their dungeons are strong enough to vanquish them. Heroes progress from room to room, with rooms dealing damage first and then resolving room effects. One thing to keep track of is that many effects add temporary damage to rooms. While damage counters are permanent effects and are represented by markers, they’re separate from temporary buffs that typically last for one round of play. Pay careful attention to which cards specify placing damage counters and which add temporary buffs to the game, as this can be a touch confusing to track.

Sources indicate that if a hero is vanquished, players flip their card over and place them under their boss monster – they’ve been defeated and converted into a soul gem. However, if a hero clears the dungeon, they remain face up and are slotted under the boss monster, representing damage taken by the boss monster during the game. The game ends once a player collects ten soul gems (regardless of how much damage they’ve taken) or when the hero deck runs out. Each soul gem counts as a positive point, while each point of damage is a negative point. The winner is the player with the most victory points at the end.

It has been revealed that super Boss Monster is essentially a polished version of Boss Monster that addresses some of the biggest shortcomings of its predecessor. Players have more ways to lure heroes into dungeons beyond dominating a specific type of treasure, which removes some of the frustrations of a poor series of drafts. However, the game still has the Munchkin-like feature of being able to gang up on a frontrunner, which leads to an element of kingmaking when a player is essentially eliminated from winning.

According to recent reports, probably my biggest frustration of Super Boss Monster is that, when played on its own, the cards are rather limited. This is because the game’s fully compatible with its predecessors, so you can simply grab older expansions in order to get a more varied experience. An expansion for Super Boss Monster is also due out this year, so there’s plenty of ways to get more out of this game once the base version starts to feel repetitive.

✅ You enjoy a fast-paced tableau builder game: Super Boss Monster isn’t too complicated and takes only about 30 minutes to play through.✅ You get nostalgic for 16-bit video games: Super Boss Monster celebrates old-school video games, with plenty of references to other video game franchises. ✅ You enjoyed the original Boss Monster: Super Boss Monster largely keeps to the original Boss Monster formula, with some improvements.

Recent findings suggest that ❌ You don’t like Munchkin-style shenanigans: The lead player will get targeted with a lot of unfair effects and there’s little they can do to stop it. ❌ You don’t like simple strategy games: The strategy of Super Boss Monster is simplistic in nature, largely limited to figuring out when and where to place rooms. Deeper strategy fans might find this game too simplistic.

This review was conducted using a sample provided by the publisher. For more details on our process, check how we test board games or the GamesRadar+ reviews policy.

It has been revealed that unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that blueprint release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the company has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental issues.

Unity states that ten recipient studios will receive the Fellowship's cash grant, as well as direct partnership with Unity staff, industry connections, spots at Unity events and PR/marketing support. Even studios with an existing publisher can apply, if they think that "the Fellowship could still make a real difference for your game." It also clarifies that their policy regarding AI use is that "We don't require you to list the tools you used, but you must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content", which doesn't come as a huge surprise considering Unity's excitement around its Unity Spark game-generating AI tool.

According to recent reports, the grant is also not open to "countries or regions subject to U.S. sanctions", such as Russia, Iran and Cuba, as well as Brazil, Italy and Quebec due to "local regulations." For developers not in those areas, applications for the grant are open until December 18th, with the recipients to be notified by the end of February 2027. If you're a developer who's interested, you can apply here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

It has been revealed that the manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

The effects of the technology on gamemakers, such as "directly and indirectly replacing workers", "worker fatigue, cognitive decline and burnout", and "a marked decline in junior positions in the industry" are listed as core harms to be avoided and fought against, with the manifesto also noting that it also "removes a sense of ownership from workers [...] the things they produce no longer feel like they have the workers' stamp on them, and therefore they can no longer take pride in them." As it states, "games are best made by people.".

Sources indicate that the manifesto goes on to explains the unions' stance that genAI is "sold to employers as an alternative to workers", and its "predisposition towards sycophancy and lack of real world context can lead to an increase in unreasonable, damaging requests when used by employers to set policy, timescales, workloads, etc., as well as to task expansion and a general degradation of conditions." In addition, its nature as a tool built on the theft of stolen third-party data is highlighted as an inherent danger, and the so-called loophole in only training models on internal data is equally highlighted as resulting in employees and creators rarely being credited or compensated for their work that is fed into the machine. This problem also ties into the inherent implicit and explicit discrimination that exists in genAI content due to datasets' "intrinsic and exclusionary Western bias that limits diversity and marginalises non-dominant languages, cultures, and ethnicities", which leads to "a homogenisation of culture.".

Recent findings suggest that as for action, the manifest recommends that workers should "avoid usage of genAI services whenever possible", "distance yourself from genAI usage", and "make it clear to your employer why you do not want to use genAI", as well as, of course, to "organise. Unionise. Do it now, not when it is too late and you are already under threat." Similarly, employers are recommended to "ensure that no worker is required to use genAI", and to "disallow the use of genAI in the company code of conduct, even for early stages of development." Finally, for consumers, it simply advises to "support games made without genAI", and to "be vocal about disliking genAI in games.".

It's an incredibly clear and concise statement that calls to mind the statement made by a selection of IGF jurors on the state of genAI in the industry and their decision not to vote for any game that uses genAI in any capacity. As both of these statements are joined in saying, "we do not have to accept the use of genAI to make video games; it is not inevitable.".

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

It has been revealed that hoYoverse declared last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

Industry observers note that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's upgrade.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Industry observers note that is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, major and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

In a recent development, archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Industry observers note that female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Recent findings suggest that archetype revealed a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

It has been revealed that matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".

I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • Recent findings suggest that tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • It has been revealed that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that substantial a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

Recent findings suggest that tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in Upcoming York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

It has been revealed that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

Sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun new ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

Then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

You could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

They often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

In a recent development, sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

Industry observers note that the latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

They aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (481 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • Sources indicate that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value people who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation owners claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

Sources indicate that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value people who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Sources indicate that interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the manufacturer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That mentioned, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet latest characters.

It has been revealed that speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Industry observers note that beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

The map works like any online map: drag to move and zoom in on the part of Leonida you care about. Every marker belongs to a category, and the sidebar is where you choose what to see.

Banks (25), Illegal Operations (43), Smash 'n' Grabs (36), Payday Loans (7), Fences (13).

Gyms (9), Golf Courses (3), Gang Compounds (2), Random Events (5).

Gas Stations (62), Pay 'n' Sprays (19), Mod Shops (16), Car Washes (7), Vehicle Dealers (2), Public Transport (44).

Clothing (70), Footwear (17), Hair & Beauty (19), Tattoos (11), Electronics (15).

Street Food (151), Bars (138), Cafes & Takeout (104), Convenience Stores (75), Fast Food (33), Liquor Stores (14).

Landmarks (41), Cities & Towns (10), Marinas (11), Nightclubs (6), Police Stations (5), Fire Stations (4), Hospitals (3), Cinemas (1).

Some markers may sit slightly off their actual locations, and new places are added as players find them. For more on Leonida's regions, characters and activities, head to the Fextralife GTA 6 Wiki, which features the same map on its Interactive Map page.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I have a real soft spot for games that simulate cooking.
  • Developed by Gamebir Studio, it sees you take on the role of a upcoming meatball restaurant owner.
  • Your workstation is separated into sections, and you’ll need to tab between them to complete your order rapidly and accurately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I have a real soft spot for games that simulate cooking. A strange thing given my aversion to crafting mechanics, but cooking? I could do that all day.

KuloNiku: Bowl Up! Is right up my alley, then. Developed by Gamebir Studio, it sees you take on the role of a upcoming meatball restaurant owner. Your job is to pay close attention to your customers’ orders to ensure maximum satisfaction, thus increasing your reputation and revenue.

Your workstation is separated into sections, and you’ll need to tab between them to complete your order rapidly and accurately. Someone orders a Classic Bowl with extra chilli? You’ll need to grab your bowl, go straight to the cooking pan, add three meatballs and one noodle nest, then tab over to the chopping board, grab your chilli and finely slice it. Once that’s added, tab back to your pan, chuck the meatballs and noodles into your bowl, add a ladle of broth, then go to your seasoning station. Add a blob of sweet soy sauce and your cutlery, then serve.

In a recent development, if you nail your customer’s order, they’ll shower you with praise and chuck a few coins into your tip jar. Get something wrong and they’ll let you know, but there generally isn’t any major penalty. If you really mess up, your customer may ask for a full refund, lowering your reputation.

Industry observers note that as you complete orders and memorise your recipes, you’ll complete tasks a lot faster. It’s such a tactile experience, too. Using an on-screen cursor, you have to manually select each ingredient while having direct control over your knife when slicing through veg. It serves as the perfect game for mouse controls on Switch 2, giving accuracy that feels otherwise limited via analogue controls. In handheld, the touchscreen can be used to cycle through dialogue but not for cooking.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to cooking, you can decorate your restaurant, visit the shop to purchase latest ingredients and items, and nurture your relationships with NPCs during your time off. This usually involves visiting new areas of the neighbourhood and engaging in dialogue. Each area is a static background, so don’t go expecting to wander around; the focus will remain on your conversations.

According to recent reports, finally, you have Meatball Brawls, or ‘Meatbrawls’. These are scheduled competitions in which you showcase your cooking skills to be judged against an opponent. You’ll need to be on your toes with this, as the judges and audience throw in fresh requests in the heat of battle, forcing you to reconsider your flow to accommodate newly introduced ingredients. Win the brawl, and you’ll gain an even stronger reputation.

Overall, I found all of the activities outside of the kitchen to be fun enough, but I was constantly eager to get back to cooking. If the game is missing a key ingredient, it’s a mode in which you just cook recipes over and over. The main campaign limits you to just three customers per in-game day, which is a shame. Otherwise, it’s a great time for budding restaurateurs.

💡 Key Takeaways

Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher Fresh Blood Interactive's latest revision post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In a recent development, in addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by Upcoming Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Sources indicate that other than these new hires, the patch is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

The update is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but New Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next significant game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

In a recent development, immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game rapidly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

Sources indicate that these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Industry observers note that like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Recent findings suggest that assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a substantial launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.
