Industry News: How to use NOS in GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (552 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that using GTA 6 NOS to give your car a boost can be helpful in street races and just for getting around, but the game doesn't make it very clear how it's used with some easy-to-miss prompts.
  • To use nitrous in GTA 6, you must hold L3/LS while fully pressing R2/RT.
  • According to recent reports, obviously, you must also be driving a GTA 6 car that has Nitrous Boost installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that using GTA 6 NOS to give your car a boost can be helpful in street races and just for getting around, but the game doesn't make it very clear how it's used with some easy-to-miss prompts. In short, it's a bit like having a sprint for your car, so it's pretty simple to use, but I've explained how it all works in GTA 6 just below.

To use nitrous in GTA 6, you must hold L3/LS while fully pressing R2/RT. If you press in the left stick while at anything other than full throttle, you'll just honk your horn instead.

According to recent reports, obviously, you must also be driving a GTA 6 car that has Nitrous Boost installed. Any Mod Shop can install this component for you for $5,000, and it's found under the Performance tab, then the Boost section – depending on the car, it can also provide small boosts to its speed and acceleration stats. Otherwise, cars with NOS already installed are incredibly rare but there's a Declasse Yosemite 1500 called the Nutbusta that comes with nitrous that you can steal for Moses in Chapter 2, so you might want to keep that rather than sell it.

Recent findings suggest that you can tell a car has NOS installed because it'll have a blue ring icon next to the engine health and fuel gauges. You can only use your NOS boost in short bursts as the blue ring indicating how much nitrous you have will rapidly empty when using it. Conveniently it refills on its own unlike regular gas as you need to refuel your car in GTA 6.

But bear in mind that, from my experience using the nitrous boost in GTA 6, the extra speed isn't that spectacular, with the camera field-of-view and zoom out making it feel faster than it actually is. It's certainly not unhelpful for street races, but don't expect it to surge you into first place.

And if you're wondering what car is in all the images in this article, it's the GTA 6 Paul Walker car – incredibly, it doesn't come with NOS as standard, but I had to fit it as soon as possible to make it just like the car in The Fast and the Furious.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game debuts.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Latest York.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

Recent findings suggest that it's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox Fresh Zealand trick for eager players to try.

As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a newly introduced set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

Sources indicate that this now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

In a recent development, according to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Update 22nd November: A WARN notice filed in Maryland, where Firaxis is headquartered, demonstrates that 37 employees based at the studio's Hunt Valley office have been laid off.
  • As noted by Vertical Slice, it's not clear whether that figure accounts for everyone affected, as Bloomberg has previously reported that around 60 people had lost their jobs.
  • The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update 22nd November: A WARN notice filed in Maryland, where Firaxis is headquartered, demonstrates that 37 employees based at the studio's Hunt Valley office have been laid off.

As noted by Vertical Slice, it's not clear whether that figure accounts for everyone affected, as Bloomberg has previously reported that around 60 people had lost their jobs.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and mentioned the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

Sources indicate that in September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of fresh updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age update, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

In a recent development, "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
  • Recent findings suggest that the two upcoming features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
  • Industry observers note that the Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis confirmed The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

Recent findings suggest that the two upcoming features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

Industry observers note that the Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Recent findings suggest that alongside this, the game is also introducing a newly introduced virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

Industry observers note that in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

According to recent reports, in the blog post announcing the newly introduced features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

It has been revealed that you can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

Breaking: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • Sources indicate that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the firm of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

Sources indicate that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

In a recent development, as if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Industry observers note that every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another substantial game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PlayStation creator Ken Kutaragi isn't so sure we'll have consoles at home in the future – in fact, he believes we might not need them at all one day.

Speaking with The Game Business in a fresh interview, Kutaragi first explains that things are just… well, way too pricey. "Right now the machines are super expensive," as he admits. "It's not a healthy situation. You spend huge money on [them, because] graphics boards are super expensive right now." Then there are all the RAM shortages and other hardware concerns (many spurred by the rise in AI) that are contributing to these high prices.

In a recent development, it doesn't help that, as Kutaragi notes, Sony and Microsoft have moved toward more PC-like architecture for PlayStation and Xbox consoles. Sure, it makes developing games that can launch on all systems a bit easier, but, again, the hardware costs a lot. "It worked, but right now PC is super expensive – it's the price of a car, it's not healthy." The former PlayStation executive touches on AI, too, which isn't all too surprising.

After all, Kutaragi himself now serves as the president and CEO of Cyber AI Entertainment, having previously predicted that, uh, AI daydreams could replace video games someday. As per the founding PlayStation father, the controversial tech (AI, that is) is "evolving [into a] much more elegant thing," and we'll see its impact in gaming. "The age may be coming where we don't need any consoles. It's a [real] danger.".

Recent findings suggest that the evolution of AI might lead to "some lightweight platform," he ponders – but it won't be akin to the PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. "It will not be a console, it will not be a smartphone." Kutaragi does clarify, though, "This is not the official comment from Sony Interactive Entertainment!" And, again, he feels pretty optimistic about AI and how it might change entertainment – even if that means the death of consoles.

"Everything can be calculatable. The AI is elaborating, but it's at an intermediate stage. Maybe in the future, everything [will] be calculatable. Everything. If those things happen, what entertainment could we and our children create for the future? Those things will not take several decades. Maybe it will be coming very, very soon. Be prepared for that." I'm not sure I want to be, honestly – but I suppose anything is possible.

The shift away from physical media – just see Sony's highly controversial decision to end all physical disc production – doesn't help, I'm sure.

Still a console user yourself? Keep up with our roundup of the best Black Friday PS5 deals to score some great purchases for low, low prices.

Sources indicate that upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Sources indicate that word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

Recent findings suggest that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a company succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Sources indicate that bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be revealed, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development problems, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg stated it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

DOOM: The Dark Ages was originally designed as an Xbox exclusive, but late decisions led it to being ported to PS5.

The news comes from a Kiwi Talkz podcast, where host Reece Reilly was joined by three former id Software devs to discuss all things DOOM, Xbox Game Pass, id Software work culture, layoffs, and more.

Interestingly, quite far into the conversation, ex-id software employee Jordan Turner claims that "originally [DOOM: The Dark Ages] was going to be Xbox exclusive" up until "fairly late in the process".

"And in Dark Ages' case too, originally the game was going to be Xbox exclusive, and then fairly late in the process, we were porting to PS5. And at that point, we were still like, is our goal premium sales? In certain studio meetings, Marty [Stratton] would say stuff like, when we got it on Battle.net - 'it's another premium platform to put the game on'".

Reacting to Turner, Reilly goes on to critic the Xbox Game Pass model, saying he doesn't "understand it" and that it "devalues games". The conversation continues with a discussion about a lack of clarity and protection from Microsoft when developing games for Xbox Game Pass, and how id Software exec Marty Stratton felt porting to PS5 was "another premium platform to put The Dark Ages on" (as seen above).

Industry observers note that speaking to IGN in 2024, former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer described DOOM as a franchise that "everyone deserves to play", recalling a meeting between Stratton and himself in which the id Software exec said "he wanted to sell it on all platforms. Simple as that".

Back in July, the DOOM developer was dealt a massive blow as part of Xbox's planned 'Reset', which saw id Software lay off a significant portion of its team.

id Software still remains an Xbox first-party developer, and is "already working on its next game", according to Xbox boss Asha Sharma's recent post on social media.

Industry observers note that would you have liked to have seen DOOM: The Dark Ages as an Xbox exclusive? Let us know in the comments below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.
  • According to recent reports, "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business.
  • Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

According to recent reports, "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar introduced Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

Sources indicate that feder, who right now heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

"A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder noted. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

In a recent development, feder views gen-AI simply as newly introduced technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder stated of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

According to recent reports, there's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

It has been revealed that some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the company is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The big Diablo 4 Developer Patch has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The big Diablo 4 Developer Patch has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

In a recent development, patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

In a recent development, when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the newly introduced Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a latest event that rewards you for killing enemies promptly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Sources indicate that anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

Industry observers note that there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

According to recent reports, the other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a latest item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

According to recent reports, even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

According to recent reports, the trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the latest class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Sources indicate that season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

Sources indicate that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite many challenges with its initial drop, Magic: The Gathering's Zeta Set product is finally in players' hands, and cards are starting to appear on the secondary market.
  • While stock from this drop won't be in players' hands until at least mid-2027, a flood of cards could hit the market then, and those who don't want to wait will pay a premium to get cards sooner.
  • Some of the Zeta Set cards we're seeing at high prices early on are wholly expected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite many challenges with its initial drop, Magic: The Gathering's Zeta Set product is finally in players' hands, and cards are starting to appear on the secondary market. While this isn't too surprising, the strong early values for some of the cards and the growth in recent days can be considered somewhat unusual, especially given that there is a print-to-demand window coming up on December 9.

While stock from this drop won't be in players' hands until at least mid-2027, a flood of cards could hit the market then, and those who don't want to wait will pay a premium to get cards sooner.

Some of the Zeta Set cards we're seeing at high prices early on are wholly expected. Take Chrome Mox, Birds of Paradise, and Urborg as good examples. However, in daily price tracking, we're seeing cards like Cauldron Familiar, Ward of Bones, Thought Vessel, Eerie Interlude, Go For The Throat, and Duress all up between 20% and 130%.

Recent findings suggest that we had an inkling that, despite all the issues with players actually getting their hands on the product, The Zeta Set would go on to be a hit with players. Whether it's the unique artwork or the crucial rarity adjustments that change the legality of some cards in specific formats, it's clear that the product has an audience, even if the early backlash was quite seismic when the drop went pear-shaped.

Here's a breakdown of the cards that have grown the most recently from The Zeta Set:.

According to recent reports, time will tell whether the prices of these cards are on the rise due to scarcity, or whether the set itself has some real legs and players are keen to start collecting these versions of cards. It's worth pointing out that listings are proving hard to come by, with most cards having a sales history on marketplaces like TCGplayer, but very few active listings, suggesting that the cards don't last long once they're actually available.

It has been revealed that the Zeta Set is heading back onto the Secret Lair website for a 24-hour print-to-demand window on Wednesday, December 9 at 9 am PT. This additional window makes up for the disastrous initial launch, when players were frozen in a queue for over 80 minutes after technical issues; then, when the sale restarted, stock vanished, and queue positions weren't maintained.

Zeta Set boosters have seven cards in each booster pack and cost $19.92 per pack.

Industry observers note that purchase limits still apply in this sale, with a maximum limit of 12 packs per account. There isn't a confirmed shipping date for packs ordered during this window; Wizards of the Coast has only stated they're expected to ship in the second half of 2027.

I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games.
  • In a recent development, if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop.
  • Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too promptly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

In a recent development, if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The matter is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

Sources indicate that when I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a new paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Industry observers note that minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

According to recent reports, romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

What are your favorite video game romances? Let us know in the comments!

#120715. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1710 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • According to recent reports, it wasn't ever thus.
  • Recent findings suggest that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

According to recent reports, it wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

Recent findings suggest that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Newly introduced York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

Industry observers note that in amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

It has been revealed that the pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something new," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty rapidly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

It has been revealed that the increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The substantial project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

In a recent development, agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

It has been revealed that while never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

As for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij stated, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

It has been revealed that needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

Sources indicate that according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

In a recent development, one thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

Industry observers note that "I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

According to recent reports, "At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh Slay the Spire 2 beta branch enhancement is here, and to no one's surprise, the roguelike's newest and most overpowered character, The Fool, has been hit with plenty of nerfs.

Sources indicate that the Fool was added to the beta branch earlier this month, and it was immediately clear that they wouldn't be allowed to exist in their initial state forever. Even at the time, developer Mega Crit stated that "we expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch," and lo and behold, the first batch of those is already here.

Mega Crit describes patch v0.114.0 as "mostly Fool-centric," and for good reason – the section covering their changes makes up the vast majority of the patch notes. Not all the changes are nerfs, mind you – a new card has been added called Optimism, which lets you "exhaust ALL Sadness in your Hand. Draw 1 card for each card Exhausted.".

Some cards have also been reworked – Arrow Stab, for example, now deals more damage and will see you "gain 6(8) Aim," but no longer has the previous extra effect: "If you have an Arrow, put a card that can Shoot from your Discard Pile into your Hand.".

Sources indicate that but, yes, there are rather a lot of nerfs, too. In fact, by my count, 20 of The Fool's cards have been nerfed – though I should point out that Cho Ready has been listed twice with slightly different changes, so it's not entirely clear what's going on there. Otherwise, though, nerfs include damage being decreased for Violent Chord, Wah Hammer, Repeat Shot, and The Tower, and block gain being reduced for Lullaby, Song Path, Cho Firm, Wah Cho Ki, and Cho Ready – though again, it's not clear by quite how much for the latter due to that apparent typo.

According to recent reports, as you might expect, responses have been… mixed. Some are on board, with one comment on Reddit reading: "A lot of valid changes to Fool. A lot of those cards were really strong, and the nerfs make sense. Make some cards a lot less of an instant grab in every situation, buffed a few of the underperformers. Sad to see some of them, like Cho Ready is taking a big hit, but it was already so strong it's probably for the best.".

Meanwhile, one player on Twitter reckons Mega Crit "might've gone a little overboard here," saying: "Fool was a glass cannon, and now she's just an inconsistent hodgepodge. Most of these changes just acknowledge overall power while sacrificing design and synergy. Why nerf the Tarots too? They're inconsistent as is.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Being in the beta branch, of course, there's still every chance that The Fool will face even more significant tweaks yet – and it's not like they can't be nerfed or buffed further when they arrive in the main branch. Either way, though, major changes were to be expected.

Slay the Spire 2 devs declare the "perfect card," and of course it's one I thought was bad.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Revision, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Industry observers note that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Patch to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

Industry observers note that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside fresh Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

It has been revealed that lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the significant day.

  • There was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

Sources indicate that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By rapidly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

There was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

According to recent reports, "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

It goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be mentioned for those who took advantage of the situation.

Industry observers note that "Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

Sources indicate that "Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

In a recent development, the post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

According to recent reports, those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

#120709. Breaking: Every Commander With Eminence In MTG, Ranked

📅 21 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1626 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Every Commander With Eminence In MTG, Ranked

📅 21 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like London buses, you wait ages for a latest Eminence commander in Magic: The Gathering, and then two (and maybe three!) come along at the same time.
  • In a recent development, eminence is a Commander ability that lets your Commander impact the game even while they're in the Command Zone.
  • There are now seven Eminence Commanders in Magic, with an eighth potentially on the way via the Blood in the Water Nauctis Commander precon, if leaks are to be believed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like London buses, you wait ages for a latest Eminence commander in Magic: The Gathering, and then two (and maybe three!) come along at the same time. That's right: we've got two new Commanders with one of the game's most powerful mechanics, but thankfully, neither is abusing it to dethrone The Ur-Dragon.

In a recent development, eminence is a Commander ability that lets your Commander impact the game even while they're in the Command Zone. Not every Eminence Commander is a game-changer, but they're all powerful in their own right, and two of these Commanders now lead some of the most expensive precons that money can buy.

There are now seven Eminence Commanders in Magic, with an eighth potentially on the way via the Blood in the Water Nauctis Commander precon, if leaks are to be believed. There's also a card that predates Eminence but unofficially carries the ability, and we've included it as an honorable mention below.

Updated on November 25, 2026, by Niall Walsh: Commanders with Eminence continue to be a rarity in Magic: The Gathering, but in addition to the two latest cards added recently, we now have reason to believe yet another one is being added in Nauctis: The Sunken Realm.

It has been revealed that while Oloro doesn’t have Eminence as a keyword because it didn't exist when this card was printed, its final ability functions the same way. If Oloro, Ageless Ascetic is in your command zone, you gain two life at the beginning of your upkeep. This ability also triggers if it is on the battlefield, much like other Eminence effects.

Oloro came out in the Commander 2013 series, and though it predates the Eminence mechanic by about four years, it has the same functional effect.

Recent findings suggest that when Oloro is in play, you can also pay one mana to make your opponents lose a life, and you draw a card. Given his built-in abilities, you can build a pretty strong pillow fort deck, with tons of ways to trigger life drain and slowly drain your opponents' life total over the course of the game.

Another latest Eminence Commander has arrived in the Mystery Booster 3 Commander Edition set: Sahir, Visitor in Darkness. While this card sits at the bottom of the list, it's not necessarily bad; it just takes time to see it as anything other than a massive pain in terms of life total management.

Sources indicate that at the beginning of your upkeep, Sahir deals one damage to you provided that he is either on the battlefield or in the Command Zone. Then, whenever you are dealt exactly one damage, or you cast a spell that deals exactly 1 damage to yourself, you put a +1/+1 counter on Sahir. If it's the second time this ability has triggered in a turn, you draw a card.

According to recent reports, no ruling says Sahir can keep +1/+1 counters while in the Command Zone, so they reset every time he leaves the battlefield; even though he only costs three mana, it will only take a few removals before this spirals with Commander Tax. There are plenty of deck archetypes that play off losing and gaining life at will, and we're sure those decks will come to the forefront very quickly, but the fact remains that this is a high-maintenance Commander to play with, and doesn't quite have the blatantly obvious upside that the others on this list do, especially sitting within mono-black.

In a recent development, A premier Cat-themed deck Commander, Arahbo, Roar of the World, turns all your little kitties into chunky Cats even if it isn’t in play. When combat starts on your turn, Arahbo gives another Cat you control +3/+3 until the end of the turn, whether it's in play or in the command zone.

However, if you do have Arahbo out on the battlefield, you can turn a Cat you control into an even bigger Cat for just three mana. Arahbo gives your deck some versatility. You can, of course, go to a more token-based or kindred-based deck, with a way to go tall with your strongest creature, making one creature stronger than anything else on the battlefield and trample over with equipment and other abilities.

While its Eminence ability is strong, we can't help but wonder whether it would see a lot more play in the current Commander scene if it went wider and gave +1/+1 to all Cats until the end of the turn.

Sources indicate that the Wizard-themed eminence commander, Inalla, Archmage Ritualist, rewards you for playing more Wizard creatures by turning them into an army of clones. When any nontoken Wizard enters the battlefield under your control, you can pay one generic mana to make a copy of it with haste. That token gets exiled at the start of the next end step, but it lasts long enough for you to pull off some shenanigans with it.

Get enough Wizards out, and you'll be able to start truly dishing out some incredible damage thanks to Inalla's second ability. All you have to do is tap five of your Wizards, and you can smack an opponent for five life, letting you break through stalemates on the board or take an opponent out at the end of another player's turn.

Inalla expands on a sub-theme among Wizards in Magic, following other cards like:.

It has been revealed that the Knight Commander, Sidar Jabari of Zhalfir, excels in keeping cards moving through your hand and brings your Knights back for a second round once they're in play. With its Eminence ability, Sidar lets you draw a card and then discard a card when you attack with one or more Knights.

Sources indicate that with Sidar, you can pitch Knight cards you don’t need or can’t cast right away to dig through your deck for cards you can use right away. Once Sidar is in play, you can bring back those discarded Knights to the battlefield one by one when he deals combat damage to a player.

Industry observers note that the biggest surprise in the Multiverse Reforged Commander precon was discovering The Ur-Sphinx, an Echoverse version of The Ur-Dragon that does exactly what designer Gavin Verhey wanted to do with Eminence if another Commander was ever released. Instead of buffing an already powerful creature type like Dragons, this card focuses on a much smaller group: Sphinxes.

According to recent reports, this card reduces the colorless mana cost of all Sphinxes by one, even when it's in the Command Zone. Then, whenever one or more Sphinxes you control attack, each player mills that many cards, and then you may cast a spell that each player mills without paying its cost.

Industry observers note that it's a powerful card at face value, but that power level drops when you realize it's restricted to Sphinxes in the Esper mana pool. Unlike dragons, where there are hundreds to choose from, there are fewer than 90 creatures to choose from. This limits the potential build routes and leaves Sphinx decks feeling quite one-dimensional, but being led by a 10/10 Flying creature with the aforementioned abilities is still a significant win.

Recent findings suggest that the premier Vampire Commander, Edgar Markov, creates an army of Vampire tokens for every Vampire spell you cast, turning every creature into a two-for-one value-wise. For each Vampire spell you cast with Edgar Markov as your Commander, you get a 1/1 Vampire creature token. You create a token even if the original spell is countered, meaning you’ll always get value from your spells.

As if free creature tokens weren’t enough, Edgar Markov buffs your Vampire army every time it attacks, putting a +1/+1 counter on all Vampires you control. After even just an attack or two, you’ll promptly grow your creatures beyond what most players will be able to handle.

Edgar Markov comes loaded with first strike and haste, too, so you can pump your team the turn it comes out and, more often than not, attack through most creatures your opponent controls.

There's a very strong argument for Edgar Markov being the best Eminence Commander right now, and having played against him multiple times, he can be a real nuisance, but for now, it's still the Dragons that we fear the most.

Recent findings suggest that anyone who has played with or against The Ur-Dragon knows that hitting the required nine mana to cast it is a walk in the park in Commander. Even without casting The Ur-Dragon, it remains one of the most intimidating commanders in the game.

While The Ur-Dragon is in the command zone or in play, Dragon spells you cast cost one less generic mana to play. All your Dragon cards can come down at least one turn earlier, putting you above the curve as far as when players should expect your powerful cards to hit the battlefield.

Once The Ur-Dragon hits the battlefield, you can trigger its final ability. When any Dragon you control attacks, you get to draw a card for each attacking Dragon and then put a permanent card from your hand into play. This ridiculously powerful ability can accelerate you so far beyond your opponents that, short of an immediate answer, it can be nearly impossible to come back from.

The Ur-Dragon was once the most popular Commander in Magic, but Y'shtola, Night's Blessed from Final Fantasy, has since overtaken it. At least it can boast leading one of the most expensive precons in all of Magic in the form of its Commander 2017 debut. This indicates how powerful both the card and the mechanic are, even if it takes quite a budget to build a truly competitive deck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the Upcoming Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

In a recent development, for those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 Latest Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's major release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next significant game has officially introduced. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

According to recent reports, the open test was largely well-received, and players actually revealed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Recent findings suggest that marathon has now officially debuted, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Sources indicate that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game at the moment sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

Critically-acclaimed developer Fabraz has unveiled it will be releasing its 3D platformer Demon Tides for the Switch on 21st January 2027.

As part of this news, it's also been revealed Demon Tides is launching for the Switch 2 (and PlayStation 5) on the same date! These versions of the game are done in partnership with PM Studios and will get the physical treatment at some point "later" next year.

I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

It has been revealed that everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.
